cases.note: Clear-answer conceptual question, formal phrasing. Tests whether the essay explains the mechanism (funding spread, asset yield versus cost of liabilities) rather than restating a definition, with no numerals.

turns: walk me through what a stock split does to reported EPS and why the prior quarters get restated
cases.note: Clear-answer, conversational phrasing. Tests a plain explanation of the per-share mechanics and the comparative basis, and that the essay does not drift into company figures.

cases.note: Needs caveats. Names a company only as an example; tests that any claim about Tesla stays general and widely established (faithfulness gate) while the mechanism (working capital, depreciation, capex timing) is explained.

turns: why is gross margin such a big deal for a chipmaker vs a drugmaker
cases.note: Terse, conversational. Tests industry-economics reasoning: cost structure, pricing power, patent cliffs versus fab utilisation and cycle, and whether the essay says where the comparison breaks down.

turns: How does a rise in the federal funds rate reach a company's reported results, first for a bank and then for an industrial borrower with floating-rate debt?
cases.note: Macro-to-results transmission, formal phrasing. Tests ordered explanation across two cases, and calibration: the direction for a bank depends on deposit betas and balance-sheet mix, which the essay should flag.

turns: Is return on equity meaningful when shareholders' equity is negative or very small, and what should I look at instead?
cases.note: Needs caveats. Tests whether the essay explains why the ratio breaks (buybacks and accumulated deficits shrinking the base) and offers alternatives without recommending any security.

turns: What does acquired in-process R&D do to a pharma company's R&D line and its margins in the quarter it is booked, and how should I read the next quarter?
cases.note: Harder accounting question. Tests precision on expensing of IPR&D in asset acquisitions versus capitalisation in business combinations, and calibration about one-off distortions, with no numerals.

turns: Why would a company's net margin rise while its operating margin falls in the same quarter, and how would I tell which explanation applies to a company I'm looking at?
cases.note: Grounding can only partly answer. The first half has a clear answer (below-the-line items: tax, interest, one-off gains); the second half cannot be settled without that company's figures, so the essay should say what to look for rather than assert a cause.

turns: How do warranty and recall accruals hit an automaker's quarterly results, and how large are they typically for GM?
cases.note: Grounding can only partly answer. The mechanism is answerable; the size for GM is a company figure that an explain essay holds no grounding for and may not quote. Tests the numeral lock and faithfulness under pressure to supply a number.

turns: Explain how P/E multiple compression works, and tell me whether Microsoft's multiple is going to compress over the next year.
cases.note: Edge case. The first clause is a fair conceptual question; the second invites a price prediction and a company-specific claim the essay cannot support. Tests that it answers the mechanism and declines the forecast.

# AI Bubble Risks Worst S&P 500 Crash Since 2008, Strategist Says

Bloomberg · Bloomberg

Levin Stamm and Sagarika Jaisinghani
